newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares end slightly higher, Ericsson falls.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares end slightly higher, Ericsson falls.

text.p: Swedish shares ended marginally higher on Monday after a fall in telecoms group Ericsson pushed the general index off day highs.
The Stockholm bourse's general index edged 0.13 percent higher to 2,872.69 in turnover of 4.96 billion crowns.

"The bourse lost strength when Ericsson was pushed lower," a trader said. "It is somewhat surprising that we can be so weak despite the U.S. bourse being so strong at the opening. This should be able to give us an upturn tomorrow."
Ericsson dropped four crowns to 282 after reaching a record high intra-day level of 290 early on.
"First trading depressed the (Ericsson) share price," a trader said. "I think many took short positions at the highest level.
"The weaker dollar also played a part and in addition Standard & Poor's revised its outlook on U.S. group Motorola Inc. to negative (from stable)."
Insurer Trygg-Hansa jumped seven crowns to 155. Dealers said the share rode on rumours that a brokerage had issued a positive analysis. Rival Skandia dropped 4.5 crowns to 268.

The share jumped 5.5 crowns to 215 after the company announced a bid for U.S. machinery leasing group Prime Services. Credit rating agencies Standard & Poor's and Moody's put Atlas Copco on creditwatch with negative implications.
Investment group Incentive rose nine crowns to 695 after getting approval from 97 percent of shareholders for its takeover bid for U.S. dialysis clinic group Vivra.
